periodic-trend.def: A property that changes in a regular way across a period or down a group of the periodic table, such as atomic radius or ionization energy.

periodic-group.def: A column of the periodic table (a group or family); its elements have the same number of valence electrons. A row is a period.

effective-nuclear-charge.def: The net positive charge a valence electron feels: the nuclear charge reduced by the shielding of the core electrons (roughly protons minus core electrons).

atomic-radius.def: The size of an atom, measured as half the distance between the nuclei of two touching or joined atoms of the element.

ionic-radius.def: The size of an ion. A cation is smaller than its atom, and an anion is larger than its atom.

electronegativity.def: How strongly an atom attracts electrons that it shares with another atom; it rises across a period and falls down a group.

electron-affinity.def: The energy change when a gaseous atom gains an electron; atoms that attract an added electron strongly release more energy.

metal.def: An element, on the left or in the middle of the periodic table, that holds its few valence electrons loosely and tends to lose them; nonmetals (upper right) tend to gain electrons, and metalloids lie between.
